title: Introduction to shape and shape grammars
central_proposition: This paper develops in detail the definitions pertaining to the shape grammar formalism for the algorithmic definition of languages of two- and three-dimensional spatial designs.

concept_definitions.name: Shape
concept_definitions.definition: A limited arrangement of straight lines defined in a cartesian coordinate system with real axes and an associated euclidean metric.

concept_definitions.name: Line
concept_definitions.definition: Determined by any set of two distinct points (end points) and always has limited but nonzero length.

concept_definitions.name: Maximal lines
concept_definitions.definition: The elements in the set of lines specifying a shape, as they are not parts of longer lines in the shape.

concept_definitions.name: Empty shape (s∅)
concept_definitions.definition: The shape specified by the set containing no maximal lines, corresponding to a blank space.

concept_definitions.name: Subshape (s1 ≤ s2)
concept_definitions.definition: Shape s1 is a subshape of s2 if and only if each maximal line of s1 is in s2.

concept_definitions.name: Identical shapes (s1 = s2)
concept_definitions.definition: Shapes s1 and s2 are identical if and only if each is a subshape of the other, meaning their sets of maximal lines are equal.

concept_definitions.name: Shape union (s1+s2)
concept_definitions.definition: The shape consisting of all lines in s1 or s2, or new lines produced by combining colinear lines from s1 or s2.

concept_definitions.name: Shape intersection (s1 • s2)
concept_definitions.definition: The shape consisting of just those lines that are in both s1 and s2.

concept_definitions.name: Shape difference (s1-s2)
concept_definitions.definition: The shape consisting of just those lines in s1 that are not also lines in s2.

concept_definitions.name: Transformation (τ)
concept_definitions.definition: Euclidean transformations (translation, rotation, reflection, scale, or compositions) that produce new shapes by changing location, orientation, reflection, or size.

concept_definitions.name: Isometry
concept_definitions.definition: A transformation that does not involve scale.

concept_definitions.name: Similar shapes
concept_definitions.definition: Two shapes are similar if one can be changed into the other by a transformation τ such that τ(s1) is identical to s2.

concept_definitions.name: Congruent shapes
concept_definitions.definition: Two shapes are congruent if the transformation τ that makes them identical is an isometry.

concept_definitions.name: Labelled point (p:A)
concept_definitions.definition: A point p with an associated symbol A.

concept_definitions.name: Labelled shape (σ = (s, P))
concept_definitions.definition: An ordered pair consisting of a shape s and a finite set of labelled points P.

concept_definitions.name: Parameterized shape
concept_definitions.definition: A shape where the coordinates of the end points of its maximal lines are variables, allowing for families of shapes.

concept_definitions.name: Shape grammar
concept_definitions.definition: A formal system with four components: a finite set of shapes (S), a finite set of symbols (L), a finite set of shape rules (R), and an initial labelled shape (I).

concept_definitions.name: Shape rule (α → β)
concept_definitions.definition: Consists of two labelled shapes, one on each side of an arrow, used to transform labelled shapes.

concept_definitions.name: Language of shapes
concept_definitions.definition: The set of all shapes generated by a shape grammar that have no symbols associated with them (i.e., labelled shapes of the form (s, Ø)).

concept_definitions.name: Parametric shape grammar
concept_definitions.definition: An extension of shape grammars where shape rules are defined by filling in open terms in a general schema, using parameterized labelled shapes.

concept_definitions.name: Shape rule schema (α → β)
concept_definitions.definition: Consists of parameterized labelled shapes α and β, from which specific shape rules can be derived by assigning values to variables.

argument_structure: The paper systematically builds the shape grammar formalism by starting with fundamental geometric concepts (points, lines, shapes), defining relations and Boolean operations on these, extending these concepts to include transformations and labelled elements, and finally integrating all these components into the formal definition of a shape grammar and its extension, the parametric shape grammar. Each definition is presented incrementally, establishing a hierarchical and comprehensive framework.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The core mechanism is the algorithmic generation of shapes through the iterative application of 'shape rules' to an 'initial shape'. A shape rule (α → β) operates by identifying an occurrence of the left-hand side (α) within a current labelled shape (γ) via a transformation (τ). This identified occurrence, τ(α), is then replaced by the transformed right-hand side, τ(β), using Boolean operations: `[γ - τ(α)] + τ(β)`. This process allows for the recursive generation of complex spatial designs from simpler components, guided by labels and geometric relationships. Parametric shape grammars extend this by allowing variables in the rules, enabling the generation of families of shapes with varying dimensions and proportions.

findings.antecedent: Specification of a shape by a finite set of maximal lines
findings.mechanism: This method prevents multiple colinear line elements from creating unlimited different specifications for the same shape, ensuring the smallest set of lines defines it.
findings.quote: This method of specifying shapes is used to ensure that the specification of a shape is unique.

findings.consequent: Subshape relation forms a partial order on sets of shapes
findings.mechanism: By defining shapes as identical if and only if each is a subshape of the other, a consistent ordering relationship is established for sets of shapes.
findings.source: Subshape and identity relations for shapes
findings.quote: When shape equality is defined by the shape identity relation, the subshape relation is a partial order on sets of shapes.

findings.antecedent: Set of all subshapes of a given shape and the subshape relation
findings.mechanism: The hierarchical structure of subshapes and their relationships, including the empty shape and all possible combinations, forms a complete and infinitely extensive representation.
findings.source: Subshape and identity relations for shapes
findings.quote: The set of all subshapes of a given shape and the subshape relation determine a lattice. This particular lattice is infinite in extent...

findings.antecedent: Set of shapes (empty shape, maximal lines, and combinations) with shape union and intersection operations
findings.mechanism: Shape union and intersection operations are closed, commutative, distributive, and have identity elements (empty shape for union, shape s for intersection), with shape difference acting as a complement, mirroring set-theoretic Boolean operations.
findings.quote: The set of all subshapes of a given shape s and the operations of shape union and intersection form a Boolean algebra.

findings.mechanism: The transformation τ is applied to the point p, while the associated symbol A remains invariant.
findings.quote: A transformation τ of a labelled point p:A is the labelled point τ(p):A, where τ(p) is the point produced by applying τ to p. The symbol associated with a labelled point is invariant under the transformations.

findings.antecedent: Transformation (τ) of a labelled shape (σ = (s, P))
findings.consequent: Produces a new labelled shape (τ(σ) = (τ(s), τ(P)))
findings.mechanism: The transformation τ is applied independently to both the shape s and the set of labelled points P.
findings.quote: A transformation τ of a labelled shape σ, σ = (s, P), is the labelled shape τ(σ) given by (τ(s), τ(P)).

findings.antecedent: Application of a shape rule (α → β) to a labelled shape (γ) under a transformation (τ)
findings.mechanism: The occurrence of τ(α) in γ is replaced by τ(β) using the Boolean operation `[γ - τ(α)] + τ(β)`, effectively subtracting the matched part and adding the new part.
findings.quote: The labelled shape produced by applying the shape rule α → β to the labelled shape γ under the transformation τ is given by [γ - τ(α)] + τ(β). This labelled shape is formed by replacing the occurrence of τ(α) in γ with τ(β).

findings.antecedent: Shape rule application where the right-hand side (β) is the empty labelled shape
findings.consequent: Erases the occurrence of τ(α) in γ
findings.mechanism: When β is empty, the `+ τ(β)` component of the rule application `[γ - τ(α)] + τ(β)` adds nothing, resulting only in the subtraction of τ(α) from γ.
findings.quote: Notice that the application of the shape rule has the effect of erasing the occurrence of τ(α) in γ whenever β is the empty labelled shape.

findings.consequent: Defines a set of shapes called a language
findings.mechanism: The grammar's rules and initial shape provide an algorithmic process for generating a finite or infinite series of labelled shapes, from which the final shapes without symbols constitute the language.
findings.quote: A shape grammar defines a set of shapes called a language. This language contains all of the shapes s generated by the shape grammar that have no symbols associated with them...

findings.consequent: Enable the definition of shape rules by filling in open terms in a general schema
findings.mechanism: Parameterized labelled shapes in the schema allow variables for coordinates, which can be assigned specific real values to define concrete shape rules from a general template.
findings.quote: Parametric shape grammars are an extension of shape grammars in which shape rules are defined by filling in the open terms in a general schema.

findings.consequent: Can define languages of shapes with proportional relationships determined in any way
findings.mechanism: Assignments to parameterized shapes can vary any spatial aspect (angles, intersections, length ratios) as long as lines remain straight, offering greater flexibility than fixed transformations.
findings.quote: Parametric shape grammars can thus be used to define languages of shapes with proportional relationships determined in any way whatever.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: A shape grammar with specific rules will generate a finite or infinite language of shapes with predictable geometric properties.
Parametric shape grammars can generate families of shapes that exhibit continuous variation in specified geometric parameters (e.g., angles, proportions).
The application of a shape rule will always result in a valid labelled shape according to the defined Boolean operations and transformations.
bridge_warrants: The distinction between shape grammars and parametric shape grammars parallels the traditional separation between Euclidean (similarity) transformations and more general transformations used in the study of spatial patterns with symmetry groups.
Shape grammars are particularly suited for defining languages of shapes with proportional relationships based on arithmetic or geometric series.
Parametric shape grammars offer a more general approach, capable of defining languages with any arbitrary proportional relationships, extending beyond the capabilities of traditional shape grammars.
model_structure: The shape grammar formalism is a generative system composed of: (1) a finite set of shapes (S), (2) a finite set of symbols (L), (3) a finite set of shape rules (R) of the form α → β (where α and β are labelled shapes), and (4) an initial labelled shape (I). Shapes are generated by iteratively applying shape rules: a rule applies if a transformed version of its left-hand side (τ(α)) is a subshape of the current labelled shape (γ). The application replaces τ(α) with τ(β) using the operation `[γ - τ(α)] + τ(β)`. Parametric shape grammars extend this by using parameterized shapes and points in the rules, allowing for variable assignments to define specific rules from general schemata, enabling greater flexibility in generating diverse shape families.
